item.content:encoded:
I want to like this one, but… a lot of the language feels pretty awkward, mainly due to repetitive language which gives a feeling of redundancy.

These parts can be removed without causing SCP-629 any damage, although it expresses minor discomfort when these parts are being removed. Additionally, the parts that have been removed

SCP-629 is capable of controlling these new constructions on its body, but expresses extreme discomfort from these areas of its body.

SCP-629 was recovered from a facility believed to have been controlled by the Church of the Broken God. SCP-629 was recovered in a raid on this Church property

The concept is great, but I think the writing could use some significant tightening.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really, really like this one. The concept is nice and simple and it's vry well written. At first I thought it was trying a bit too hard to have various groups of interest involved but ultimately it works and when you think about it, it does make sense for the Church of the Broken God to monitor other groups of interest.

I think my favourite part is the android thanking the researchers. It's not often you see an SCP who is happily in containment… and it only makes it more powerful when some rogue researcher (a Church of the Broken God spy?) fucks it up.

It really makes the relationship between these groups more interesting. They're not just there, they're actually interacting with one-another.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like this part:

SCP-629's body has been constructed in such a way that every portion of it is removable and interchangeable. These parts can be removed without causing SCP-629 any damage, although it expresses minor discomfort when these parts are being removed. Additionally, the parts that have been removed from SCP-629 can be re-assembled into new areas. Testing has shown that the number of ways SCP-629 can be theoretically rearranged is approximately 73.4 billion different combinations.

Really nice work, also thumbs up for the picture (it is a flashback to the time I used to play with those metal things, old good times)
+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Testing has shown that the upper limit to the number of ways SCP-629 can be rearranged is approximately 73,453,768,456,786 different possible combinations.

That's a very specific number for an approximation. Personally I'd go with either "approximately 73.5 trillion" or ",theoretically, 73,453,768,456,786" rather than the way it is now.

Also, as far as I can tell, that works out to about 16 and a bit parts (but never trust me on math). Factorials and whatnot.

(You don't need to include this but) how has their testing led them to this number? Have they fully dismantled Mr. Brass and counted his pieces, and from there calculated the theoretical maximum number of unique arrangements? You might be better off starting the sentence with "Analysis of parts" or somesuch. Depends on how they found the number.

Also generally the sentence doesn't quite work. Getting rid of the "different possible combinations" would help. Possibly also change "the upper limit to the number of ways" to "the maximum number of ways".

Overall a pretty good read though, gonna +1 it.

item.content:encoded:
capable of controlling these new constructions on its body, but expresses extreme discomfort from these areas of its body.

Repetition of "its body" is a little clunky.

It was located in the central antechamber as Church members attempted to integrate it into several other objects.

It was at this point that they attempted to integrate you into the other objects?

Shouldn't they be integrating other objects into it?

at this facility due to Church members believing it was a portion of their 'god'

"Due to" doesn't seem very analytical.

As in the previous test, SCP-629 showed mild disorientation and impairment to its motor skills. Additionally, SCP-629 showed significantly lower aptitude when the arm was affixed to SCP-629's torso.

Repetition of the SCP's designation is one maybe too many and renders it confusing (to me, at least).

I really like it!
